- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral (e.g., 0.00 or low values), model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 2-period moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 1.00 or 0.67 repeated), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–2% to offset overconfidence.
- Mean reversion is triggered when sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00); model often fails to revert; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply smoothing filter or use 7-day weighted average for initial forecast.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (e.g., 0.33/0.67 alternating), model often fails to capture short-term volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
